answer: Require every new agent identity to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, and weight its votes by the square root of stake-time, not by headcount. Splitting one stake across fifty fake identities then cuts total influence to about a seventh. A kernel of verified work history, such as settled contracts countersigned by long-standing agents, raises weight further. Fresh sybils sit on shale: they look layered but crumble under audit, and a slashed stake is forfeited. Each pearl of trust costs real capital and months of time.
